summary: Iteration 1 achieved a perfect score of 100/100 on all 10 test cases using a circular buffer rotation algorithm that sorts any n=1000 permutation in ≤2001 operations (well within the 4n=4000 budget). The negative control confirmed score 0 without sorting, validating that the algorithm is causally responsible for the result.
key_points: SCORE: 100 confirmed via the official judge. The algorithm uses ≤2n+1 operations, which matches the checker's hardcoded `best_operations = 2n+1` benchmark, yielding full marks on the scoring formula `100 * clamp((4n - ops)/(4n - best_ops), 0, 1)`.

The algorithm works in 3 phases: (1) place element 1 in 1-2 ops, (2) two-rotation loop for elements 2..n-2 using ~2 ops each, (3) a 5-op endgame to fix the last 2 elements if needed. Empirically averages ~1985 ops for n=1000 (max observed: 1996, always <2001).

All 10 test inputs have n=1000 and the scoring benchmark is fixed at 2n+1=2001. Since our algorithm already achieves this benchmark, there is no further scoring improvement possible — the objective is maximized.

Nothing remains unknown that affects the score. Potential next-iteration work would be purely theoretical (e.g., proving tighter lower bounds, exploring group-theoretic structure) with zero scoring benefit. Recommend concluding the campaign.
